clue.text: Change locals — what are the options?

parts.note: to change something is to alter it
the locals of a place are its natives

explanation.surface: Someone weighing up what the people of a place could be swapped for, asking what choices there are.
explanation.definitionFit: Options and alternatives are synonyms: both are the choices open to someone.

clue.text: A driver perhaps made it!

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be arranged another way, signalling an anagram

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A motorist, presumably, has got to their destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' looks like it qualifies 'A driver', but it signals an anagram of the letters of A DRIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To have made it is to have got there, so the past tense of reach a destination fits.

clue.text: A brutal chopping of a list

indicators.note: chopping cuts the words up, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone savagely cutting down a list of items.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabular describes data set out in rows and columns, as in a table or list.

clue.text: Greeting one after 26?

explanation.surface: A welcome extended to someone who follows the puzzle's last clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 across is TYING THE KNOT, a wedding; the party held after a wedding is the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception is a welcome given to a guest, and also the celebration held after a marriage ceremony.

clue.text: Allow Frenchman into entrance to mine

indicators.note: into signals that one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance to a mine
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a French title for a man

explanation.surface: Permitting a Frenchman to go into the mouth of a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance to mine' looks like 'first letter of mine' but means a whole word, ADIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to let them in, so allow is a synonym.

clue.text: One covers half of shin with more confidence

indicators.note: half of takes just part of the word shin, here its second pair of letters

parts.note: surer means more confident

explanation.surface: Someone protecting part of a leg, feeling more assured.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurance company covers clients against loss, so it is the one that provides cover.

clue.text: Issue call-up to returning English volunteers

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word call is read bottom to top

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

indicators.note: returning means the following pieces are read backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A summons to join up sent to English volunteer soldiers coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call-up' looks like conscription, but it is NAME written upwards, EMAN; 'returning' turns ETA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to come out or flow from a source, which is what emanate means.

clue.text: Give a lift to fool

explanation.surface: Offering someone a ride in order to trick them.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone for a ride is literally to drive them somewhere, and idiomatically to deceive or cheat them.

clue.text: A tiresome person comes back in charge of vigorous exercise

indicators.note: comes back means the word for a tiresome person is read backwards

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person

explanation.surface: A dreary individual returns to lead a workout session.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobic exercise is sustained, strenuous activity that raises the heart rate.

clue.text: Loses place accepted by young girl

indicators.note: accepted by means one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: a miss is a young girl
to lay something is to put or place it down

explanation.surface: A young girl takes in a location that someone has misplaced.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislay something is to lose it by forgetting where it was put.

clue.text: Dismisses broadcasts on boxing

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to broadcast a signal is to send it out
boxing goods up is packing them

explanation.surface: Someone transmitting programmes about prizefighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' suggests the sport, but here it means putting into boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone packing is an idiom for getting rid of them abruptly.

clue.text: Pen love letters and get hug!

indicators.note: the letters of the words pen love are taken and set out afresh

explanation.surface: Write a romantic note and receive an embrace in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' looks like correspondence, matching 'Pen love', but it tells you to use the letters of PEN LOVE in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to wrap around completely, as an embrace does.

clue.text: Coach carrying royal to the ground

indicators.note: carrying means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a train is made up of coaches, so coach suggests train
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of the Queen

explanation.surface: A carriage bringing a member of the royal family down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a bus or a trainer; here it stands for TRAIN, which wraps ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features, the lie of the ground.

clue.text: Rank obtained in commission

explanation.surface: A military rank granted when an officer is commissioned.
explanation.definitionFit: An order is a class or grade, such as an order of knighthood, and also an instruction to supply goods, a commission.

clue.text: Singers who have risen from disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in a jumble, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Vocalists who have made a comeback after catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singers' means people who 'sing' to the police, not vocalists; the letters of RISEN FROM are reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, to sing is to inform on accomplices, so singers are police informants.

clue.text: Poorly rated commercial system?

parts.note: read the other way round, the second word of the entry is a set of letters that, freed up, become the word rated, which is what poorly rated asks for

explanation.surface: An economic arrangement that gets low marks.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: taking FREE as an anagram signal, FREE TRADE says 'TRADE, loosened', i.e. RATED jumbled, which 'Poorly rated' describes. The question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Free trade is international commerce without tariffs or quotas, an economic arrangement.

clue.text: A bread roll twist perhaps is plenty

parts.note: a bun is a small bread roll
the twist is a 1960s dance, so it is one example of a dance

explanation.surface: A plaited loaf or bun of bread comes in large quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' looks like a twisted bread shape; it is the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance means a great quantity, more than enough, which is what plenty means.

clue.text: Completely turning turtle on the fourth of July?

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means the first piece sits on top of the second
turning means the letters of turtle are spun into a new order
fourth of picks out the fourth letter of the word July

explanation.surface: A turtle flipping over during the American Independence Day holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning turtle' is an idiom for capsizing, but here 'turning' rearranges TURTLE to UTTERL; 'the fourth of July' is not the holiday but its fourth letter, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterly means totally or absolutely, a synonym of completely.

clue.text: Latin lover put on one, we hear!

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word one is replaced by a word that sounds like it

parts.note: the Spanish name Juan is said much like the English word one

explanation.surface: A Latin American romeo dressed up, according to gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: Spanish JUAN is pronounced roughly 'hwan', close to 'one'. 'Latin' here means Spanish-speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Juan, the legendary Spanish seducer, is a byword for a womaniser, a Latin lover.

clue.text: Gone to a course in Italy

parts.note: something gone is in the past

explanation.surface: Having left to follow a route in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a route, but it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is a staple dish served as a course of an Italian meal.

clue.text: Continue working to support the newspapers

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece that supports another sits underneath it

parts.note: the press is the newspapers collectively
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Keep going at the job so as to keep the papers afloat.
explanation.definitionFit: To press on is to carry on resolutely, so continue is a synonym.

clue.text: Main source of crystals?

parts.note: main is the old poetic word for the sea, so this asks for a crystalline seasoning taken from the ocean

explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' reads as 'chief', but it is the sea; evaporated seawater leaves salt crystals.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt obtained by evaporating seawater forms crystals, so the ocean is literally their source.

clue.text: Means to put cares behind at home

indicators.note: behind means the cares piece comes after the at home piece

parts.note: someone at home is in
to tend someone is to care for them

explanation.surface: Planning to forget one's worries while staying in.
explanation.definitionFit: If someone means to do something they plan it, as one who intends does.

clue.text: The smell of endless money in America

indicators.note: endless means the end letter of the money word goes round to the front

parts.note: cents are small change in American money

explanation.surface: The odour of limitless wealth in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' looks like 'infinite', but it means the end letter moves: CENTS becomes S + CENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent is an odour, so it is the smell of something.

clue.text: In which one might stretch the truth?

definitions.text: In which one might stretch the truth?

parts.words: In which one might stretch the truth?
parts.note: an idiom for lying is read literally: a medieval torture device stretched prisoners to force a confession

explanation.walkthrough: 'stretch the truth' means to exaggerate, but here the victim is stretched to extract the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: The rack was a frame on which a victim's body was stretched to force them to tell the truth.

clue.text: Missing the start, fourteen got lost on the way

indicators.note: got lost suggests the letters wander into a different order
missing the start means the first letter of fourteen is dropped

explanation.surface: A group of fourteen, absent at departure, went astray during the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing the start' removes F from FOURTEEN, leaving OURTEEN, which 'got lost' rearranges. 'fourteen' looks like a cross-reference to 14 across, but it is the plain word.
explanation.definitionFit: En route is French for on the road, meaning during the journey.

clue.text: Avoid a black spot

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a stain is a spot or mark

explanation.surface: Stay away from a dark blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from something, to keep away from it.

clue.text: Getting granny ready for wedding?

parts.note: a granny is a kind of knot, so preparing one means fastening it, and the idiom for this is the phrase for getting married

explanation.walkthrough: 'granny' looks like a grandmother being dressed for a family wedding; it is the granny knot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tying the knot is an idiom for marrying, and literally describes fastening a knot such as a granny.
